{"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "For each fiscal year, compute year-over-year growth in inventory (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (item COGS). Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal year with at least a 6-month reporting lag.", "rationale": "Inventory accumulating faster than sales signals weakening demand and future markdowns/writeoffs, a form of over-investment that the market underprices.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than COGS)"},
{"name": "Accrued-to-Cash Earnings Ratio", "construction": "Compute the difference between reported net income (Compustat NI) and operating cash flow proxied as (net income + depreciation/amortization DP - change in non-cash working capital derived from balance-sheet items ACT, LCT, CHE, DLC). Scale by average total assets (AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June with a reporting lag.", "rationale": "Earnings driven more by accruals than cash are less persistent and often reflect aggressive accounting, so high-accrual firms subsequently underperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (cash-heavy earnings)"},
{"name": "Capital Expenditure Intensity Reversal", "construction": "Compute capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) scaled by lagged net property plant and equipment (PPENT), then take the deviation of the current year's ratio from the firm's own prior three-year average. Rank cross-sectionally each June with a reporting lag.", "rationale": "Firms sharply increasing investment relative to their history tend to overexpand into declining opportunities, leading to lower subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (declining relative capex)"},
{"name": "Gross Margin Momentum", "construction": "Compute gross margin as (SALE - COGS)/SALE for the most recent fiscal year and the year prior; take the change. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June by the year-over-year change with a reporting lag.", "rationale": "Improving gross margins signal strengthening competitive position and pricing power not yet fully reflected in prices.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (rising gross margin)"},
{"name": "Idiosyncratic Return Volatility", "construction": "Each month, regress a stock's daily excess returns over the prior 60 trading days on the CRSP value-weighted market excess return; take the standard deviation of residuals as idiosyncratic volatility. Rank cross-sectionally at month end.", "rationale": "Under-diversified investors and limits to arbitrage cause high-idiosyncratic-volatility stocks to be overpriced and subsequently underperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low idiosyncratic volatility)"},
{"name": "Dollar Trading Volume Illiquidity", "construction": "For each stock compute the average daily absolute return divided by daily dollar volume (price times shares traded) over the prior 12 months using CRSP daily data. Rank cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "Illiquid stocks require a return premium to compensate investors for higher transaction costs and price impact.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (more illiquid stocks)"},
{"name": "Share Issuance Change", "construction": "Compute the log growth in split-adjusted shares outstanding (CRSP shares times cumulative adjustment factor) over the prior 12 months. Rank cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "Net share issuance reflects managers exploiting overvaluation and dilutes existing holders, predicting lower future returns; net repurchasers outperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (net repurchasers/low issuance)"},
{"name": "Asset Turnover Improvement", "construction": "Compute asset turnover as SALE/average total assets (AT) for the latest fiscal year and prior year; take the change. Rank cross-sectionally each June with a reporting lag.", "rationale": "Rising asset efficiency signals improving operational productivity and future profitability that the market prices with delay.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (improving asset turnover)"},
{"name": "52-Week High Proximity", "construction": "Each month compute the ratio of a stock's current price to its highest closing price over the prior 52 weeks using CRSP data. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Anchoring on the 52-week high causes investors to under-react to good news near the high, so stocks close to their high subsequently outperform.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (price near 52-week high)"},
{"name": "Financial Leverage Change", "construction": "Compute total debt (DLC + DLTT) scaled by total assets (AT) for the latest and prior fiscal year; take the change. Rank cross-sectionally each June with a reporting lag, controlling by industry.", "rationale": "Firms rapidly increasing leverage face heightened financial distress risk and constrained flexibility, predicting lower subsequent risk-adjusted returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (deleveraging firms)"}]}
